title: Iran’s Guard Says It Hit a U.S. Radar in Bahrain; CENTCOM Says Two Drones Were Shot Down
dek: Iran’s Revolutionary Guards claim a strike on a U.S. radar in Bahrain; CENTCOM says two drones were downed with no injuries and denies the radar was destroyed. Houthis claim Aramco attacks.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: U.S. Navy photo of officials and commanders at Naval Support Activity Bahrain, a U.S. base in Manama
image.credit: U.S. Naval Forces Central Command / U.S. Fifth Fleet, via Wikimedia Commons

keyPoints: CENTCOM said two one-way attack drones launched by Iran’s IRGC toward Bahrain were shot down, with no injuries or damage.
The IRGC said it had targeted and destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike in Sirik; CENTCOM called that claim false.
Iranian media attributed the Sirik strike to an “enemy” attack; the Guardian reported it was a U.S. airstrike on a telecommunications tower.
Yemen’s Houthis claimed drone and missile attacks on Aramco and other Saudi targets; the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted drones. Meridian has not verified the claims.
body:
U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) said Friday that it shot down two one-way attack drones that Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) launched toward Bahrain, with no injuries or damage. The statement came hours after the IRGC said it had targeted and destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar installation in Bahrain. CENTCOM called that claim false, [Anadolu reported](https://aa.com.tr/en/americas/centcom-denies-iranian-claim-of-attack-on-us-radar-in-bahrain-says-2-drones-shot-down/4124158).

## The IRGC’s account

The IRGC said the strike was retaliation for an attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, a port city in Iran’s Hormozgan province. Iranian state news agency IRNA, citing official sources, said Sirik had been hit by an “enemy” strike on Thursday. Iranian authorities use that term for the United States and Israel. The Guardian reported that the tower was hit in a U.S. airstrike ([The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/13/iran-us-radar-bahrain-sirik-hormuz)).

In a statement carried by the semi-official Tasnim news agency, the IRGC called its action a “serious warning” to stop what it described as aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. It said its aerospace force was in “full readiness to engage without limits” if the actions continued, [Al Jazeera reported](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/13/iran-says-it-struck-us-radar-site-in-bahrain), citing Reuters.

## Claims that could not be confirmed

The Guardian described the IRGC claim as Iran’s first direct attack on U.S. military installations in months. Al Jazeera’s correspondent in Tehran said Iran had not previously answered U.S. strikes on its communications networks by targeting U.S. military assets in the region. Al Jazeera’s reporter at the White House said neither the U.S. nor the Iranian account could be independently confirmed ([Al Jazeera live coverage](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/13/iran-war-live-riyadh-china-discuss-houthis-as-group-claims-aramco-attacks)).

## What CENTCOM said

CENTCOM’s post on X said the IRGC “launched two one-way attack drones toward Bahrain and both were shot down by U.S. forces. There were no injuries or damage” ([CENTCOM on X](https://x.com/CENTCOM/status/2121225254446018729)). The Guardian reported that CENTCOM also denied that the radar had been destroyed.

## Houthi claims against Saudi targets

Yemen’s Houthis made separate claims against targets in Saudi Arabia. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said in Telegram statements that a drone had targeted the Aramco company in Riyadh and that the operation had achieved its objective. He also claimed a drone attack on a military cargo plane at Sharurah Airport, a ballistic missile strike on Khamis Mushait Air Base and a drone attack on pumping station number 7 of the East-West pipeline, [Republic World reported](https://republicworld.com/world-news/houthis-claim-drone-strikes-on-riyadh-saudi-military-sites-coalition-says-drones-intercepted-2026-11-13-140951), citing ANI.

The Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a drone in the Eastern Region and a drone launched by the Houthis in the Riyadh area. Meridian has not verified the Houthi claims or any damage at the sites they named.

Al Jazeera’s live coverage also reported that Riyadh and China had discussed the Houthis. That discussion is attributed to Al Jazeera alone in this story, because no second account was available when this story was written.

## Background

The United States and Israel launched a war on Iran on Feb. 28. Tehran responded with missile and drone attacks across the region and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, Anadolu reported. A memorandum of understanding signed in June to pave the way for a final peace deal later collapsed amid disagreements, including over navigation in the strait.

The Guardian reported that President Donald Trump said in a series of media interviews over the past day that he would attack Iran only if necessary. He also claimed that Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia, had urged him to hold back from planned large-scale strikes.
